title: Married priests
hookLine: Eastern Catholic priests are often married

lines: A PRIEST WITH A SON AT HIS HEM.
A WOMAN WITH A TITLE OF HER OWN.
cards: Sunday, after the Divine Liturgy, in a parish hall that smells of coffee. The priest is still in his black cassock, and a small boy is tugging at its hem, asking for a donut. His own son.

Across the room a woman pours coffee and greets newcomers by name, and people call her by a title of her own. For a Latin Catholic visiting for the first time, it's a double take. A married Catholic priest?
Nobody here is breaking a rule. This is an Eastern Catholic parish, in full communion with Rome, doing what its tradition has long done.

teach.b: The New Testament doesn't hide that the apostles had families. Mark's Gospel says, in the Douay-Rheims, "Simon's wife's mother lay in a fit of a fever," and Jesus heals her. Simon is Peter.

Peter had a mother-in-law, so Peter had a wife. And when Paul lists what a bishop should be, he writes that he must be "blameless, the husband of one wife." Today the Catechism sets two disciplines side by side.
In the Latin Church, priests are normally chosen from men who live a celibate life and intend to keep it, for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.
In the Eastern Churches a different discipline has been in force for many centuries: bishops are chosen only from celibates, but married men can be ordained deacons and priests.
Both, the Catechism says, are honored. Neither is called second best. The order of things surprises people.
A man marries first, and then may be ordained.

teach.h: THE PRIEST'S WIFE HAS A TITLE.
teach.b: A priest doesn't go looking for a wife after ordination; if a single man is ordained, he stays single. And the woman at the coffee urn?
Her life is shaped by her husband's calling too: the late phone calls, the shared table, the move to a new parish.

teach.h: BLAMELESS, THE HUSBAND OF ONE WIFE.
teach.b: Greek speakers call her presbytera. In Arabic-speaking parishes she is khouria. Ukrainians have their own word for her, and so do Russians.
Her title is spoken with respect.

how: In the Eastern Catholic churches married men may be ordained deacons and priests, provided they marry before ordination; bishops are chosen from celibate clergy. In the Latin Church, priests are normally celibate.

games.q: you're a single Byzantine Catholic seminarian, soon to be ordained, and you hope to marry someday. what does your church's tradition say?
o: get ordained now and marry later.
marry first, or be ordained and stay single.
you must become a monk to be ordained.
games.why: in these churches marriage comes before ordination, never after. married men may be ordained priests, but a priest does not marry once ordained.

practice: Hold a priest's family in mind: a married Eastern priest, a deacon and his wife in a Latin parish, or a pastor of any church who comes home tired to people who love him.

Picture their kitchen table on a Sunday night, and let your attention rest on the one who usually gets thanked least. If you pray, simply say, Lord, have mercy, for that household; if you don't, just wish them a quiet evening.

wordCard.voice: Married priests. In the Eastern Catholic churches, married men may be ordained priests, a discipline the Catechism calls long-standing. They marry before ordination, never after.

orig.note: Greek, as Greek-speaking Christians say it today: the priest's wife.

carryVoice: Your line: the priest's wife. A calling is often shared at the kitchen table. Until tomorrow.
